question.problem: Find the values of $x$ that satisfy $7x>-7$ and $3x<3.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection. 

- First, we solve $7x>-7\,:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}7x & >-7 \\ \frac{7x}{7} & >\frac{-7}{7} \\ x & >-1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/9b902e22e6808cf01993494e199b9fcbd184d084e385ef94cb9a1953c00abb7c.png)

- Then, we solve $3x<3\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & <3 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & >\frac{3}{3} \\ x & <1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/ca26af3420f15a115c44ddb234afe4226e850799b5f91625faaee4c4fad37a4a.png)

$$

$$

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/12b3a4dedd88b66e7c06812b83c3195e889bdf22d40e45432e8569aaf5764047.png)

$$

$$

Thus, the final solution is $-1<x<1.$
